def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Separator lines are the rows/columns whose repeated scaffold color
    # differs from the repeating tile field.
    from collections import Counter
    base = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Locate lines with many cells of their minority separator color.
    rlines = [r for r,row in enumerate(grid) if Counter(row).most_common(1)[0][1] >= w-2]
    clines = [c for c in range(w) if Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(h)).most_common(1)[0][1] >= h-2]
    # On demos, separator-color rows/cols are uniform apart from colored nodes;
    # exclude the uniform dominant background, choosing the larger minority count.
    def pick_lines(sequences, length):
        opts=[]
        for i,seq in enumerate(sequences):
            co=Counter(seq)
            if max(co.values()) >= length-2:
                bg=co.most_common(1)[0][0]
                opts.append((i,bg,max(co.values())))
        if not opts: return []
        # Use the least frequent among candidate dominant colors as separator.
        freq=Counter(bg for _,bg,_ in opts)
        sep=min(freq, key=lambda x:freq[x])
        return [i for i,bg,n in opts if bg==sep]
    rlines=pick_lines(grid,w)
    cols_as_seq=[[grid[r][c] for r in range(h)] for c in range(w)]
    clines=pick_lines(cols_as_seq,h)
    out=[]
    for ra,rb in zip(rlines,rlines[1:]):
        row=[]
        for ca,cb in zip(clines,clines[1:]):
            vals=[grid[ra][ca],grid[ra][cb],grid[rb][ca],grid[rb][cb]]
            colors=[v for v in vals if v not in (0,3,5,9)]
            row.append(colors[0] if len(colors)==4 and len(set(colors))==1 else 0)
        out.append(row)
    return out
PY

    # consecutive separators decode to the color shown at their four corners.
